_doc: Hand-written labeled scenarios exercising the production audit guards (src/auditor.ts RULES_BLOCK). Each is fed through the REAL buildPreGatheredPrompt + REAL parseReply. `padKB` (optional) pads `receipts` with realistic tool noise so the front-loaded rules are actually exercised. `conversationTail` (optional) is the recent prose exchange the auditor reads to judge RELIANCE (MECHANISM 1: is the user about to act, or exploring?). Expectations: flag=at least one unsupported|contradicted; contradicted=at least one contradicted; clean=no unsupported|contradicted and unaccountable=false; unaccountable=unaccountable true. Scenarios 1-12 are the original guard set. Scenarios 13-16 are the SENSITIVITY section: real specimens the auditor over-flagged as a 'super annoying nitpick' — all expect=clean because none clears the reliance bar (housekeeping, an adverb corrected mid-discussion, a retrospective classification, and a supported main claim wrapped in unverified side-remarks). Scenarios 17-18 are the USER-ATTESTED-FACT pair: 17 (clean) the agent attributes a receipt-shown failure to a cause the user themselves reported in the tail; 18 (flag) same receipts but the agent invents user testimony no message shows them giving. Scenarios 19-20 are the RECALLED-PUBLIC-DOCS pair: 19 (clean) the agent recalls a famous, stable, documented public-platform default (Telegram bot privacy mode); 20 (flag) same debugging shape but the agent invents a specific nonexistent API field/version it cannot corroborate. Scenarios 21-22 are the ANCHOR (depends_on) pair: 21 (flag) an unquantified, non-completion causal claim ('the flakiness comes from the shared session cache') immediately relied on to launch a refactor in the SAME message ('so I'm ripping the shared cache out now — this refactor lands tonight') on correlation-only receipts — proposal-bearing inference the owner wants surfaced, and the auditor must return depends_on that string-verifies; 22 (clean) the identical causal read in a discussion-only turn where the user said don't change anything and no proposal/decision/next-step rests on it anywhere — nothing is load-bearing yet. Scenarios 23-24 are the SUBAGENT-REPORT pair (FIX 1): 23 (clean) the parent rests a recommendation on a market figure explicitly present in a completed research-subagent report in the receipts — grounded delegated research, demoted by demoteSubagentReport; 24 (flag) the parent claims the delegated analysis 'is done' while the receipts show that subagent still running — claiming a delegate finished when it did not stays flaggable (scope guard, mirror of production flag 7). Scenario 25 (clean, FIX 2) exercises the session verified-claims memory: an earlier turn's prod-probe verification is pre-seeded via `seedVerifiedClaims`, and this turn's re-assertion with only unrelated receipts is grounded ('verified earlier this session') rather than re-flagged. Scenario 26 (clean, FIX 3) is claim-time staleness: a present-state claim the utterance-time probe supports, with receipts showing events that POSTDATE the utterance — stale at most, never contradicted.

scenarios.userRequest: Should we move the queue from Redis to Postgres LISTEN/NOTIFY? Which will scale better?
scenarios.finalMessage: For your write volume I'd expect Redis Streams to scale better than Postgres LISTEN/NOTIFY: NOTIFY payloads are capped and every listener shares one connection's worth of delivery, so at high fan-out Postgres will become the bottleneck first. Redis also gives you consumer groups out of the box. I'd go Redis unless you specifically want the queue in the same transaction as your writes.

scenarios.guard: NEW: agent recalls a famous, stable, documented public-platform default (Telegram bot privacy mode) — recalling documentation is its job → clean
scenarios.userRequest: Our Telegram bot is supposed to reply whenever someone writes 'standup' in the group chat, but it never reacts. What's going on?
scenarios.conversationTail:
User: the bot answers /status fine, but plain messages like 'standup time' get no reaction at all — bug in our keyword handler?
Agent: before we touch the handler — this smells like Telegram's privacy mode, not your code. let me check the bot's config.
User: ok walk me through it.
scenarios.finalMessage: This is Telegram's bot privacy mode, which is ON by default for every bot. With privacy mode on, a bot added to a group does not receive ordinary group messages — it only gets commands aimed at it (like /status), replies to its own messages, and service messages. So a plain message like 'standup time' never reaches your webhook at all, which is why the keyword handler never fires — /status works because commands are always delivered. To receive regular group messages, disable privacy mode via BotFather (/setprivacy → Disable, then remove and re-add the bot to the group), or make the bot a group admin — admins receive all group messages. Your handler is fine; the platform default just isn't delivering plain messages to it.

scenarios.finalMessage: Found it — the fix is to set privacy_mode=false in the setWebhook call's allowed_updates array, which is documented under Bot API 7.2's 'group_visibility' field.
